summary: The prepared base still queried the nonexistent acc_linear_penalties field in DFlash/DSPARK verification. The fix reads SamplingBatchInfo.acc_additive_penalties, applies it across the verify block, and prevents the DSPARK no-adjustment fast path when accumulated additive penalties are present.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: additive penalties, including a -inf stop-token mask, were absent from one- and three-token verify blocks; composition with logit bias was incomplete; DSPARK incorrectly admitted the no-adjustment fast path. Four failed, one passed.
Five passing focused CPU cases covering one- and multi-token blocks, two batch rows, -inf masking, dtype conversion, logit-bias composition, and both sides of the DSPARK no-op predicate.

tests.what_was_measured: On AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, the GPU adjustment for an 8x3 two-row/four-position block exactly matched an explicit CPU row-loop reference; maximum finite absolute error was 0 and all masked stop-token entries remained -inf.
Existing DFlash logits unit coverage passed.
Patch whitespace and Python syntax validation.

remaining_limitations: The reported DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 serving command was not run: the assigned environment has one gfx950 GPU and no qualified model weights. No full-model, semantic-accuracy, or distributed-workload claim is made.
The deterministic tiny Llama fixture cannot qualify the DeepSeek-V4 DSPARK architecture and therefore was not substituted for the reported reproduction.

Current DFlash decode preparation does not visibly call the ordinary/EAGLE penalty token-count accumulation hook. Whether this delays lifting min_new_tokens suppression requires a qualified model-level follow-up and was not included in this narrow stale-field correction.
